column1: TS: return 'parsed value OR error' without throwing?
column2:
A discriminated-union Result:
  type R = { ok: true; value: X } | { ok: false; error: string };
Caller checks .ok (narrows the union), acts. Return DATA, don't reply/throw inside
-> no hidden I/O on the error path, stays unit-testable.

column1: TS: type guard (x is T) vs assertion (as T)?
column2:
GUARD: a function returning `s is T` that VERIFIES at runtime, then narrows.
  function isSlug(s: string): s is Slug { return LIST.includes(s); }
AS: just asserts to the compiler — no check, can lie (rest as [Slug] when rest is string[]).
Use the guard. `arr.filter(isSlug)` narrows string[] -> Slug[] honestly.

column1: TS: strict integer parse from a string (reject '123abc', '12.9')?
column2:
Number.isInteger(Number(raw))  -- Number() is strict: '123abc'->NaN.
parseInt() is LENIENT: parseInt('123abc')->123, parseInt('12.9')->12 (truncates).
zod equivalent: z.coerce.number().int()  (coerce = Number(raw); .int() rejects NaN/floats).

column1: Refactor: why extract parseChatId separately from resolveManagerCommand?
column2:
Layering: parseChatId is PURE and reusable by commands that DON'T want auth
(/addmanager parses a chatId but can't require an existing manager).
resolveManagerCommand composes the manager-membership check ON TOP.
Extract the smallest reusable floor; build domain logic above it.

column1: Prisma: avoid fetching a row's id just to use it in a where/create?
column2:
Filter/connect via the RELATION instead:
  find:    where: { userId, role: { name: MANAGER } }        // findFirst, no role.id fetch
  create:  data:  { role: { connect: { name: MANAGER } } }   // connect by unique name
  filter:  where: { revokedAt: null, role: { name: MANAGER } }
Skips the separate lookup entirely.

column1: Prisma: type a param that accepts the base client OR a transaction (tx)?
column2:
type Client = PrismaClient | Prisma.TransactionClient;
Prisma ships TransactionClient = Omit<PrismaClient, ITXClientDenyList>
(deny list: $connect $disconnect $on $transaction $use $extends).
Don't hand-roll the Omit — it drifts from Prisma's list across versions.

column1: Prisma: fix a read-modify-write lost-update race on a set of rows?
column2:
Don't read-the-whole-set -> modify -> rewrite-the-whole-set (two concurrent runs clobber).
Do ONE atomic single-row op and use the returned count as the 'did it change' signal:
  add:    createMany({ data:[row], skipDuplicates:true })  // count 0 = already there
  remove: deleteMany({ where:{...} })                       // count 0 = wasn't there
Needs @@unique on the row. Absolute-set replace (setX) is only for 'user gave the full set'.

column1: When is reading-then-writing a race vs safe?
column2:
Reading to DECIDE a write  = race: concurrent readers compute from stale state -> lost update.
Reading to DISPLAY after a write = safe: you're not mutating based on it.
So: re-fetch the list to SHOW it post-mutation is fine; re-fetch to COMPUTE the next write is the bug.
